criteria.title: Bahia remains a backup control plane
criteria.given: backup functionality is added to Bahia
criteria.when: operators define policies, recipes, repositories, runs, restores, retention, replication, or verification
criteria.then: Bahia orchestrates workflows and provenance while external backends own snapshotting, repository formats, deduplication, transfer, compression, and encryption primitives

criteria.title: Backup workflows are Nostr-native
criteria.given: a backup or restore workflow is requested
criteria.when: Bahia processes historical and realtime workflow events
criteria.then: it uses scoped REQ subscriptions, EVENT handlers, EOSE for catch-up, OK verification for publishes, CLOSED handling, AUTH handling when required, event validation, dedupe, and idempotent correlation tags instead of polling or timeout-based completion

criteria.title: Backup recipes are portable orchestration artifacts
criteria.given: an operator defines a backup recipe
criteria.when: the recipe contains quiesce, snapshot, export, verify, resume, restore, or replication steps
criteria.then: the recipe references backend adapters and resource tags without embedding backend-specific repository formats or hardcoded production credentials

criteria.title: Signed provenance is produced for every backup run
criteria.given: a backup run reaches a terminal state
criteria.when: Bahia publishes the terminal run and verification events
criteria.then: the signed provenance identifies what was backed up, who initiated it, backend and repository identifiers, hashes or backend snapshot identifiers, verification status, restore-test status when available, relay publish outcomes, and rejection reasons for failures

criteria.title: Verification-first policy is enforceable
criteria.when: snapshot creation succeeds but verification or restore testing fails or is skipped
criteria.then: Bahia marks the backup unverified and policy consumers cannot treat it as a verified restore candidate

criteria.title: Backend adapters are real and explicitly bounded
criteria.given: a backup runtime adapter is configured
criteria.when: Bahia invokes CreateSnapshot, VerifySnapshot, Restore, ListSnapshots, DeleteSnapshot, or Health
criteria.then: the adapter calls the real backend API/CLI or returns an explicit unsupported/configuration error; production paths do not use fake, stub, placeholder, or filesystem_mock behavior

criteria.title: Restore workflows are approval-aware and auditable
criteria.given: a restore request targets infrastructure, data, deployments, models, or stateful services
criteria.then: Bahia records approval or rejection as signed Nostr events before adapter execution and publishes restore result provenance after verification

criteria.title: Backup Nostr namespace is non-conflicting and documented
criteria.given: backup implementation slices consume backup Nostr events
criteria.when: they allocate command, result, status, observation, read-model, or attestation kinds
criteria.then: they use the documented backup namespace: commands 38400-38409, terminal results 38410-38419, status/observations 6981-6984, replaceable read models 31991-31999, and attestations 31310-31311

criteria.title: Backup definitions are the operator-facing registry abstraction
criteria.given: an operator defines fleet backup intent
criteria.when: the intent is persisted in Bahia registry state
criteria.then: a BackupDefinition composes repository, policy, recipe, schedule metadata, tenant/environment/owner scope, approval policy, restore target rules, executor targeting fields, labels/grouping, and audit fields without implementing execution handlers in this slice

coverage_notes: The U4-1 docs/protocol slice resolves the namespace ambiguity; backup-run, restore, and retention slices now wire the relevant Nostr command/status/result/read-model contracts into reactor, responder, projector, and app composition.

Restore request and approval events 38402/38403 use the existing reactor validation/dedup/authorization/EOSE/CLOSED/AUTH path; required approval gates adapter execution and BackupRestoreState 31998 is projected.

Retention enforcement event 38404 uses backend-native adapters, publishes progress as BackupObservation 6984 and terminal BackupRetentionResult 38414, and intentionally does not add a retention execution read model.
The allocated namespace avoids the known collisions: 31200 remains artifact signature attestation, and 38395/38396 remain AI/ML terminal result kinds.
BackupDefinition domain model and backup_definitions migration added for bahia-gbo2; handlers, MCP, UI, scheduling execution, and executor placement remain tracked in dependent Beads.
